inventory.bf_lotNo: Passion fruit, Grapefruit, Strawberry, Dank. Strata, formerly known as X-331, is Indie Hop’s first hop variety to be released out of the Oregon State Aroma Hop Breeding Program in Corvallis, Oregon. Born in 2009, Strata is the progeny of an open pollinated Perle located in an Oregon State experimental field at Corvallis, Oregon. From the get-go, this hop was out to impress. Between its strong disease resistance, vigorous growing habit, and complex layers of aroma, x331 rose to the top of an impressive group of competitors.

inventory.name: Mosaic
inventory.bf_lotNo:
order  306274
The aroma/flavor descriptors for the wildly popular Mosaic hop commonly include fruity (blueberry), citrus (tangerine, grapefruit), tropical (mango, guava), floral, and earthy. The combination of these aroma/flavor descriptors with the relatively high alpha-acid levels allows this hop to serve a dual purpose, as both a bittering and flavor/aroma hop in the brewing process. Ultimately, Mosaic provides flavor and aroma profiles in beer that simply cannot be accomplished with other hop cultivars.

inventory.name: Saaz
inventory.bf_lotNo: Saaz hops are the famous landrace variety from the Czechia region, but this is specifically US Saaz, grown by our friends at Virgil Gamache Farms in Toppenish, WA. US Saaz caries some of the same floral and spicy elements as Czech Saaz, but this American-grown lot presents with brighter citrus and a hint of cherry. US Saaz hops work well in classic European styles and lagers, but also fits perfectly in new twists on those styles. Aroma: Classic noble aromas. Floral, citrus, and spice. Typical Analytical Range Alpha: 3.0-5.0% Beta: 4.0-6.0% Total Oil: 0.3-1.0 ml/100g US SAAZ HOP SUBSTITUTIONS US Saaz is the obvious choice to replace the scarce Czech grown Saaz. US Saaz hops carry similar characteristics and flavor profiles as East Kent Golding, US Golding, and Hallertau Mittlefrüh making these hops an excellent substitution in your next light lager.

inventory.name: Servomyces
inventory.bf_lotNo:
Servomyces stands out as the best yeast nutrient containing zinc for beer yeasts.
Why Servomyces?

It's a zinc-enriched inactive yeast (Lallemand product) providing bioavailable zinc (0.15-0.5 ppm target in wort) bound in yeast hulls, protecting it from wort chelation—unlike plain zinc salts. This speeds fermentation, prevents stuck ferments, boosts yeast health/growth, and improves beer quality in high-gravity or stressful conditions.
Key Benefits for Beer

    Dramatically faster starts and healthier yeast metabolism vs. inorganic zinc.

    Supports all beer styles, especially lagers/high-ABV/adjunct-heavy.

    Adds trace minerals (magnesium too) beyond just zinc.

Dosage: 1g per 100L wort (10 ppm), added to boil or cold side. Pairs well with other nutrients.

inventory.name: Wyeast Beer Nutrient Blend
inventory.bf_lotNo: Wyeast Beer Nutrient Blend is a custom blend of vitamins, minerals, and micronutrients required for yeast cells to carry out an orderly and complete fermentation from start to finish. A wort that is nutrient-deficient, or which has adequate nutrients but limited bioavailability to the cells, can experience inhibited yeast growth, disrupted or incomplete fermentations, inconsistent attenuation rates from batch to batch, and diminished cell viability. Supplemental nutrients are always beneficial, but especially valuable during yeast propagation and stressful fermentation conditions (e.g. high-adjunct worts, high-gravity fermentations).

inventory.name: Diammonium Phosphate (DAP)
inventory.bf_lotNo:
DAP is sometimes used with beer yeast but isn't typically the first choice for standard all-malt beer fermentations.
When Recommended

Most all-malt worts naturally provide sufficient Yeast Assimilable Nitrogen (YAN, usually >250-300 ppm), so DAP supplementation is rarely needed for healthy beer yeast strains. It's more commonly recommended for challenging beer scenarios like high-gravity worts (>8% ABV), high-adjunct/sugar washes (e.g., seltzers), or nutrient-poor extracts to prevent stuck ferments and off-flavors like H2S.
Better Alternatives

Beer brewers often prefer complete yeast nutrients like Fermaid K/O, Wyeast Nutrient, or Servomyces over pure DAP, as these provide a broader nutrient profile (amino acids, vitamins, sterols) beyond just nitrogen. Pure DAP works as a nitrogen boost but lacks these extras, making it more wine/mead/cider-oriented.
Dosage for Beer

If using DAP, stick to ½ tsp (about 1.5g) per 5-gallon batch, added late in the boil—equivalent to roughly 0.13-0.2 g/L. Split additions (50% early, 50% mid-ferment) for high-gravity beers to avoid excess yeast growth
